# Unassumed

> AI rehearsal for first-time founders. Unassumed turns a rough idea into named
> assumptions, rehearses the customer conversations that could break them, and
> scores the founder's questions rather than the founder's idea.

Unassumed is a pre-launch product from London. The site is currently a single
landing page with a waitlist. The private beta opens in November 2026.

## What it does

- **Scribble** — a note, a voice memo or a photo of a napkin becomes a first-pass
  business model canvas the founder can argue with.
- **Assumption** — every block on that canvas becomes a claim with a status.
  Yellow means believed but unproven.
- **Rehearsal** — the founder practises a customer interview against a synthetic
  customer that objects, digresses and refuses to be led.
- **Evidence** — what a real person actually said is logged with its source, and
  assumptions that stop surviving are marked contradicted.

## The position it takes

Unassumed does not score ideas and does not issue a "validated" verdict. A
language model cannot know whether a company will work; it can tell when a
founder is fishing for a compliment. Simulation is rehearsal. Only a real
customer is evidence. The method draws on lean startup practice and *The Mom
Test* — ask about past behaviour, not hypothetical future behaviour.

## Pages

- [Landing page](https://unassumed.com/): the product, the method, and the waitlist.
- [Privacy notice](https://unassumed.com/privacy): what happens to an email address given to the waitlist.
